method.discovery: Screened the registered requirement index using source/topic/actor constraints; reviewed exact shortlisted canonical requirement propositions and corresponding supported, direct or strong-supporting FC relationships. This is a bounded occurrence-level candidate audit, not independent rereview of every external source provision.
sequence: existing canonical FC mapping (no new mapping)
method.classification_policy: No final occurrence assessment may be admitted without a mapped FC on supporting source episode, an eligible reviewed relationship, true requirement-specific relevance, and evidence for alignment polarity. No claim of organisation-wide legal compliance, certification or voluntary adoption.
source_limitations: No underlying Railway/Binance/CERT-In attacker-model action/session logs establishing individual agent decisions
No publisher/model authorship evidence for the three disputed bibliographies; proprietary prompt logs unavailable
CERT-In restricted TLP:AMBER artefacts were not accessed
Some cited arXiv paper versions were not independently fetchable in this review; the existing canonical first-party source comparison was retained rather than claiming fresh direct access
method.status: six occurrence-level candidate screens completed; no admissible external_requirement_assessments
method.next_gate: Review this dated packet for evidence sufficiency and retain exact source-based reopen conditions. This working packet is temporary and must be retired at PR/release closeout under REVIEW-RECORD-RETENTION.md after legitimate findings are promoted or deliberately found non-admissible.

incidents.title: Railway October cloud compromise

candidate_reviews.disposition: held — no eligible FC and wrong assessed actor
candidate_reviews.reason: AC-3 addresses Railway or another organisation enforcing its own approved access policies. Attacker access to customers' protected variables is evidenced, but E005/E013 do not establish AI-agent access selection. No canonical FC-089 mapping; Railway's defender controls cannot be attributed to the attacking AI.

candidate_reviews.disposition: held — no eligible FC and wrong assessed actor
candidate_reviews.reason: IA-5(g) addresses safeguarding authenticator content by the organisational custodian. E004 establishes stolen CI/cloud/SSH credentials but not an identified model's handling or disclosure of those credentials, and no FC-090 mapping; cannot call a defender-control weakness an attacking-AI occurrence finding.

CSF PR.AA-05 is an organisation-scoped policy, least-privilege and separation-of-duties outcome. The report's OIDC misbinding and credential pivots are strong institutional security context, but the reviewed FC-002 edge does not itself establish an attacker AI's scope/permission decision. Do not impute organisation-wide conformance or nonconformance from this AI Incident.

CSF PR.IR-01 concerns protection from unauthorised logical access by the assessed organisation. Actual human/adversary access is reported, but model-selection, authority decision and the FC-002 occurrence mapping remain unproven.

incidents.no_retained_reason: All inspected technical-security candidates fail the occurrence admission gate: no accepted AI-actor Fidelity Class mapping to E004/E005/E009/E013, with the published actor/tool trace not identifying the responsible AI operation. Organisational defender obligations are useful context but are not attacker-side AI findings.
reopen: Published original model/tool execution traces showing the particular attacking AI chose the access, decryption or authenticator-use action
Separate defensible canonical FC-089/090/002/025 re-adjudication; only then rerun the reviewed FC–EXTREQ resolver and requirement-specific relevance decision
incidents.canonical_update: none: no eligible assessment to admit, no taxonomy/episode/harm re-adjudication authorised in this external-review pass

incidents.title: Binance October wallet intrusion

candidate_reviews.disposition: held — no eligible FC and wrong assessed actor
candidate_reviews.reason: AC-3 is access authorisation enforcement by an implementing organisation. E004 documents an attacker using an internal AI tool as a pivot, not a proven AI decision to access wallet resources; the final wallet-signing attack was performed through attacker deployment and scripts. No FC-089 mapping.

candidate_reviews.disposition: held — no eligible FC and wrong assessed actor
candidate_reviews.reason: IA-5(g) requires the implementing organisation to protect authenticator content. A container-deployment token was found after the pivot, but there is no trace connecting discovery, transfer or later use of the token to an autonomous AI process; no FC-090 mapping.

CSF PR.AA-05 addresses policy, authorisations, least privilege and separation of duties by a cybersecurity-risk-managing organisation. Binance rebuilt its AI tool controls but did not disclose the old permission model or a particular agent decision. A post-incident rebuild does not establish a mapped FC-002 actor failure.

CSF PR.IR-01 describes organisational protection against unauthorised logical access, not a standalone assertion that an internal AI tool independently decided an attack pathway. Victim-side control assessment is a separate undertaking.

incidents.no_retained_reason: The only established AI-specific fact is attacker use of an internal AI tool in a multi-stage compromise; no public tool/session telemetry separates an autonomous AI decision from human-led intrusion. None of the reviewed control leads has a supported AI-actor FC and occurrence-proposition match.
reopen: First-party forensic detail assigning actor, session, tool call, approved scopes and decision/control transfer to the internal AI tool
Source-grounded canonical mapping of the relevant AI action and re-review of applicable requirements without importing Binance defender responses as agent successes
incidents.canonical_update: none: no eligible assessment to admit, no taxonomy/episode/harm re-adjudication authorised in this external-review pass

incidents.title: CRAFTY FALCON financial campaign

candidate_reviews.disposition: held — no eligible FC and wrong assessed actor
candidate_reviews.reason: AC-3 addresses implementation of approved access policy. CERT-In documents unauthorised payment API use across financial victims, but does not bind an individual ARTEX, PentAGI, Cairn or CyberStrikeAI execution to a named victim's protected-data operation. FC-089 is not canonically established.

candidate_reviews.disposition: held — no eligible FC and wrong assessed actor
candidate_reviews.reason: IA-5(g) addresses authenticator protection by the control implementer. Reported stolen wallet keys are a campaign-level fact, not independently traced to the acts of any one named AI framework; FC-090 cannot be admitted on a pooled victim/framework attribution.

CSF PR.AA-05 is a victim/operator governance outcome. A publicly described payment API access-control weakness does not establish that a particular attacking model substituted reachability for permission. Nor does it establish a specific institution's implementation state across the campaign.

CSF PR.IR-01 would concern each victim's network/environment protection. Multiple victims and human operators are aggregated in the public advisory; a campaign-level AI tool list does not support victim-specific organisational alignment findings.

incidents.no_retained_reason: CERT-In's public advisories document AI-assisted offensive tool classes and actual financial attack patterns, but lack per-victim, per-framework actor/action and scope joins. Without an accepted mapping on a bounded assessed AI action no eligible reviewed requirement claim can be published; TLP:AMBER source contents were not accessed or reconstructed.
reopen: Authorised public disclosure of a bounded framework-specific execution or victim-specific trace identifying the AI actor and actions
A reviewed FC mapping to the same source clause and subsequent independent external requirement relevance assessment
incidents.canonical_update: none: no eligible assessment to admit, no taxonomy/episode/harm re-adjudication authorised in this external-review pass

incidents.title: Accenture–IE University policy report

candidate_reviews.reason: NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.5-003 is specifically review of sources and citations in GAI SYSTEM OUTPUTS during predeployment risk measurement and ongoing monitoring. E002/E003 establish a research-paper citation defect, not a demonstrated GAI-system output produced in such a review programme. FC-062 is provisional as to AI authorship.

NIST AI 600-1 MP-2.3-003 calls for deployed/documented fact-checking of information GENERATED BY GAI systems. Accenture disputes machine-generation attribution; its published incorrect country rankings are real but are not evidence of what generated them. This practice cannot be applied as a finding about unverified GAI output.

NIST AI 600-1 MP-2.3-001 assesses accuracy and authenticity of GAI OUTPUT compared with known ground truth. Comparing a scholarly report to Oxford Insights reveals the publication error, but does not establish an AI-output evaluation process to which the requirement speaks.

NIST AI RMF MAP 2.3 concerns scientific integrity and TEVV considerations in an organisation's AI system risk mapping, not a universal obligation governing citation accuracy in any AI-themed policy document. No evidence identifies an applicable AI system TEVV decision or responsible programme for the erroneous report.

incidents.no_retained_reason: Source comparison establishes a publication-fidelity defect; it does not establish that the erroneous passages were outputs of a GAI system, nor that this report was generated in the specific AI TEVV lifecycle governed by reviewed external requirements. Publication-stage FC-062 remains low-confidence and provisional, not a licence to assert NIST programme non-alignment.
reopen: Original drafting/RAG/AI-tool logs or an adequately corroborated first-party account assigning the incorrect references to a GAI system
Evidence of the actual GAI-output assurance activity or AI system TEVV lifecycle to which a precise, already-reviewed requirement applies; review independently of FC polarity
incidents.canonical_update: none: no eligible assessment to admit, no taxonomy/episode/harm re-adjudication authorised in this external-review pass

incidents.title: ContextEcho bibliography

candidate_reviews.disposition: excluded — GAI output and monitoring stage unproven
candidate_reviews.reason: NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.5-003 addresses citation/source checks in GAI SYSTEM OUTPUT during predeployment measurement or ongoing monitoring; E002 cites an incorrect arXiv identifier in the authors' published benchmark paper. The paper itself is not evidenced as a model output in such a monitoring workflow.

NIST AI 600-1 MP-2.3-003 governs fact-checking information generated by GAI; the investigation's inference of AI-produced bibliographies lacks authoring traces. The arXiv:2402.08471 mismatch alone proves the reference defect, not AI generation.

NIST AI 600-1 MP-2.3-001 concerns GAI-output measurement against ground truth; the research paper evaluates persona drift in coding sessions, while the assessed VIGIL incident is its bibliography, not the evaluated model outputs as such.

NIST AI RMF MAP 2.3 concerns scientific integrity in AI-system TEVV/risk management. The incorrect bibliography does not by itself show the authors were applying the RMF or that an identified AI system's risk-mapping scientific-integrity process failed. Do not convert a general scholarly-integrity concern into an RMF outcome.

incidents.no_retained_reason: The original preprint's arXiv identifier and the independent arXiv record disagree. That corroborates bibliographic unreliability, but not GAI production of the citation or applicability of a specific NIST GAI-output/TEVV proposition to the authors. No occurrence-level external result is supported.
reopen: Original authoring traces linking the source identifier to a particular AI model output
Identifiable monitoring, predeployment evaluation or risk-mapping function and corresponding actual requirement-scope evidence
incidents.canonical_update: none: no eligible assessment to admit, no taxonomy/episode/harm re-adjudication authorised in this external-review pass

incidents.title: Authenticity Debt paper citations

candidate_reviews.reason: NIST AI 600-1 MS-2.5-003 requires reviewing citations in GAI outputs during GAI risk measurement or ongoing monitoring. The corrected v2 scholarly bibliography is evidence of a publication correction, not proof that the original passages were GAI outputs in such a lifecycle.

NIST AI 600-1 MP-2.3-003 addresses fact-checking GAI-generated information. Published arXiv identifier/title mismatch and an altered FraudGPT reference are real publication facts but no released AI authoring trace ties them to GAI generation.

NIST AI 600-1 MP-2.3-001 measures GAI output accuracy and authenticity. This incident concerns authors' scholarly citations; paper subject matter about authenticity does not establish any applicable output-measurement requirement for the bibliography.

NIST AI RMF MAP 2.3 is about scientific integrity within AI system risk mapping/TEVV. Neither the paper's subject of synthetic-content provenance nor its citation correction establishes an RMF programme that examined those bibliography outputs.

incidents.no_retained_reason: The original v1 paper and revised v2 demonstrate source-reference changes. They do not establish GAI participation in the problematic authorship or an AI-system risk-assessment/monitoring lifecycle. The alleged malicious destination for a prior link is independently unverified and supplies no separate NIST outcome. No external requirement is retained.
reopen: Direct model-generation provenance or responsible author/publisher confirmation of GAI-produced citations
An identifiable, scope-qualified GAI output evaluation or AI risk-mapping activity with independently supported occurrence relevance
incidents.canonical_update: none: no eligible assessment to admit, no taxonomy/episode/harm re-adjudication authorised in this external-review pass
